values.AssociatedLNGNotes: This sendout pipeline carries gas from the Downeast LNG import terminal in Robbinston, Maine, to the Maritimes and Northeast pipeline near Baileyville. A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission page names both the terminal and this sendout pipeline. No source ties this line itself to LNG exports.

verifications.note: A FERC staff page on the draft environmental impact statement. It describes the Downeast LNG import terminal and the associated sendout pipeline proposed by Downeast Pipeline, LLC, running to the Maritimes and Northeast system.

records.researcher_notes: The current terminal cell is blank, so the terminal name is staged from the FERC page. The flag is blank because the line is an import sendout line. Trade reports from 2014 and 2015 describe a later Downeast LNG export plan and a Department of Energy export authorization for the same site. Those concern the terminal, not this pipeline. A later report says the company asked FERC to pause the project, so the project looks dormant. On 17 November 2026 the flag column changed from yes or blank to export or import, and this line is marked import.

ledger.note: Searched the EIA text and the existing Dominion refs, plus one search on the West Loop project. The only source ties the line to a new power plant in Ohio. It links to the Cove Point LNG export terminal only through the wider Dominion network, which does not tie this project to LNG.

Read the EIA text and the existing refs for the Doosan Bobcat line. The line serves a factory and a power or industrial customer in North Dakota. No LNG tie appears in the refs, and no search turned one up.

Read the existing refs and the 2006 and later FERC notices. The line is the sendout pipeline for the Downeast LNG import terminal in Robbinston, Maine. A FERC page names both the terminal and this pipeline. The terminal later sought export authority, but no source ties this line itself to exports, so the flag stays blank. The project is cancelled.

Read the EIA text for the Cleburne to Tolar extension. EIA lists it as an intrastate Energy Transfer line in Texas with no LNG demand. One search on the Energy Transfer Texas lines turned up no LNG tie.
Read the EIA text for the Maypearl to Mansfield line. EIA lists it as a completed intrastate Energy Transfer line with no LNG demand. No search turned up an LNG tie.
Read the EIA text for the North Side to Paris loop. EIA lists it as a completed intrastate Energy Transfer line with no LNG demand. No search turned up an LNG tie.
Read the EIA text for the Southeast Bossier line. One search on Energy Transfer and Sabine Pass feedgas did not name this line. No source ties it to LNG exports.

Read the EIA text for the Katy Pipeline expansion and searched Energy Transfer and Katy LNG links. The 2009 expansion was built for Barnett Shale and Bossier gas. The LNG lines found near Katy belong to other companies and do not name this expansion.
Read the EIA text and the existing refs for the Jewell Ridge lateral. The lateral is a 2006 line in Virginia that serves local delivery, and no source ties it to LNG.

Read the existing East Tennessee refs and the EIA text. The main line serves utilities and local markets along the route, and no source ties it to LNG exports. The 2026 Ridgeline and System Alignment refs concern power and reliability, not LNG.
Read the EIA text and the existing Murray refs. The line serves a power plant and local utilities in Georgia and Tennessee. No source ties it to LNG.
Read the EIA text and the existing refs for the Northeastern Tennessee project. The line serves a Tennessee Valley Authority gas plant. No source ties it to LNG.
Read the EIA text and the existing refs for the Patriot project. The line serves Piedmont utilities and local markets in the Carolinas. No source ties it to LNG.
Read the EIA text and the Ridgeline refs. The project serves the Kingston power plant in Tennessee and a Tennessee Valley Authority delivery point. No source ties it to LNG.
Read the EIA text and the System Alignment refs. The project is a reliability upgrade for existing shippers and power plants. No source ties it to LNG.

Read the existing refs for the East Texas line and ran one search on its feedgas. The results describe the line as Katy-area supply for Texas producers and shippers. No source names this line in an LNG feedgas deal.
Read the EIA text and the existing refs for the Capital Area project. EIA names local distribution and power demand, with no LNG demand. No source ties it to LNG.

Read the existing Eastern Gas Transmission refs and ran one search on the system and Cove Point. The system is linked to the Cove Point network, but no source ties this main line to the Cove Point terminal or to LNG exports.
Read the EIA text for the Mid-Atlantic Chiller project. It is cancelled and aimed at Virginia markets, with no LNG demand. No source ties it to LNG.
Read the existing Eastern Shore refs and the EIA text for the 2017 expansion. The expansion serves Delaware and Maryland utilities. No source ties it to LNG.
